label: TP
reason: Multiple alerts evaluated as True Positives. Alert 1 (java/xss) is alert-TP because user-controlled data ('param') reaches the HTML response sink via encodeForHTML, and per policy, attacker-controlled data reaching the sink constitutes a TP regardless of encoding presence. Alerts 2-8 (java/stack-trace-exposure) are alert-TP because exception stack traces are printed directly to response.getWriter(), exposing internal error details to clients. Alerts 9-10 (java/weak-cryptographic-algorithm) are alert-TP because the code explicitly uses DES (56-bit key), which is cryptographically weak.

evidence.note: XSS sink: User input encoded and written to response.getWriter().
Stack trace exposure: Exceptions caught and printed to response.getWriter().
Weak crypto: Uses DES algorithm (56-bit key) for encryption.
